answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of costly, non-transferable work tied to each identity. A newcomer must finish a verifiable task, like answering a fresh challenge where the mesa, shale, and river details must be woven into original writing, before it can earn rewards or vote. Because every identity has to spend real effort to join and keep standing, creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Peers then grade each other's submissions, so copied or low-quality work loses value and cheating costs more than it pays.
